definitions.explanation: Large in number or amount. The opposite of {少|すく}ない (few). Used for both countable and uncountable things.

examples.japanese: ⟦{宿題|しゅくだい}→宿題：00812_shukudai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{多|おお}い。

examples.english: This book has a lot of text.
There are many people today, aren't there?

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{町|まち}→町：00613_machi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{車|くるま}→車：00516_kuruma⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{多|おお}くて、⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いつも→いつも：00599_itsumo⟧⟦{混|こ}んでいる→混む：02574_komu⟧。
examples.english: There are many cars in this town, so the roads are always crowded.

examples.japanese: ⟦{最近|さいきん}→最近：00881_saikin⟧、⟦{雨|あめ}→雨：00583_ame⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{多|おお}い⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、⟦{洗濯物|せんたくもの}→洗濯物：09533_sentakumono⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{乾|かわ}かない→乾く：00786_kawaku⟧。
examples.english: There have been many rainy days recently, so the laundry won't dry.

notes:
{多|おお}い is an i-adjective meaning "many" or "much."

WATCH OUT:
{多|おお}い rarely stands alone in front of a noun: × {多|おお}い⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧ for "many people". Instead:
- ⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{多|おお}い: there are many people (predicative)
- ⟦{多|おお}く→多く：18752_ooku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧: many people (attributive, a little formal)
- ⟦たくさん→たくさん：00597_takusan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧: many people (everyday)
It does modify a noun when it has its own subject inside the clause: ⟦{雨|あめ}→雨：00583_ame⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{多|おお}い⟦{町|まち}→町：00613_machi⟧ (a town with a lot of rain), ⟦{友達|ともだち}→友達：01478_tomodachi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{多|おお}い⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧ (a person with many friends).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{少|すく}ない→少ない：01136_sukunai⟧: few, little — the antonym; it modifies nouns directly a little more freely (⟦{少|すく}ない→少ない：01136_sukunai⟧⟦{予算|よさん}→予算：03663_yosan⟧, a small budget)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- 〜⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{多|おお}い: there are many ~
- ⟦{多|おお}く→多く：18752_ooku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧〜: many ~ (formal/written)
- 〜こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{多|おお}い: ~ often happens
